WITH _base AS (
  SELECT
    customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
    customers.tier AS "orders.customers.tier",
    COUNT(*) AS "orders.n"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
    ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
  GROUP BY
    customers__regions.name,
    customers.tier
), _cm_orders__net_sum AS (
  SELECT
    customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
    customers.tier AS "orders.customers.tier",
    CAST(SUM(CAST(orders.amount - customers.discount AS DOUBLE)) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.net_total"
  FROM orders AS orders
  LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
    ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
  LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
    ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
  WHERE
    NOT customers.id IS NULL
  GROUP BY
    customers__regions.name,
    customers.tier
)
SELECT
  _base."orders.customers.regions.name",
  _base."orders.customers.tier",
  _cm_orders__net_sum."orders.net_total",
  _base."orders.n"
FROM _base
LEFT JOIN _cm_orders__net_sum
  ON _base."orders.customers.regions.name" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_orders__net_sum."orders.customers.regions.name"
  AND _base."orders.customers.tier" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM _cm_orders__net_sum."orders.customers.tier"
LIMIT 21

args.message: For each order I took the amount minus the ordering customer's discount (the discount is a flat amount per customer). I then added these up by region name and customer tier. Each row also shows the total for its whole region. I left out the 6 orders that have no customer, which leaves 5,010 orders. Customers with no known region are grouped under a null region; only silver-tier customers fall into that group, with 10 orders.
